graph.definition: A structure made of a set of vertices and a set of edges, where each edge connects two vertices. In this module, graphs are finite, undirected, unweighted and simple: no edge connects a vertex to itself, and at most one edge connects any pair of vertices.

vertex.definition: A basic element of a graph, drawn as a circle. Also called a node.

edge.definition: A connection between two distinct vertices. In an undirected graph, an edge can be followed in both directions.

neighbor.definition: A vertex is a neighbor of another when an edge connects them.

path.definition: A sequence of vertices in which each consecutive pair is connected by an edge. Its length is the number of edges it contains.

cycle.definition: A path that starts and ends at the same vertex, uses at least three edges and repeats no other vertex.

traversal.definition: A systematic process that visits every vertex reachable from a starting vertex exactly once.

bfs.definition: A traversal that uses a queue to visit vertices in order of their distance from the starting vertex, measured in number of edges.

dfs.definition: A traversal that follows edges as deep as possible from the most recently discovered vertex, backtracking when no undiscovered neighbor remains. It can be implemented recursively or with an explicit stack.

queue.definition: A first-in, first-out (FIFO) collection: elements are removed in the same order in which they were added.

stack.definition: A last-in, first-out (LIFO) collection: the most recently added element is removed first.

frontier.definition: The data structure holding the vertices the traversal still has to work on: the queue in BFS, the stack in DFS.

connectedComponent.definition: A maximal set of vertices in which every pair is connected by a path. A traversal from a starting vertex reaches exactly the vertices of that vertex's connected component.

isolatedVertex.definition: A vertex with no edges. It forms a connected component on its own.

startVertex.definition: The vertex where a traversal begins.

undiscovered.definition: State of a vertex the traversal has not yet reached.

discovered.definition: State of a vertex the traversal has reached and added to the frontier, but has not yet started processing.

processing.definition: State of a vertex whose neighbors the traversal has started, but not finished, examining.

processed.definition: State of a vertex whose neighbors have all been examined. The traversal does not return to it.

visited.definition: General term for a vertex the traversal has reached. Because it is ambiguous, this lab distinguishes discovered, processing and processed vertices.

shortestPath.definition: In an unweighted graph, a path between two vertices that uses the fewest edges. BFS finds shortest paths from the starting vertex in this sense; this does not apply to weighted graphs.
